title: LLM agents lack advanced reasoning and memory
problem: Developers are frustrated that current AI agents, despite advancements, still struggle with complex reasoning, long-term memory, and consistent performance. This limits their ability to handle nuanced tasks and maintain context over extended interactions, affecting the reliability and utility of agentic AI applications.

title: Difficulty integrating LLMs with existing tools and data
problem: Developers face challenges in seamlessly integrating LLMs and AI agents with existing software, particularly for tasks like reading and editing common file formats (e.g., Microsoft Office files) or accessing structured data. This requires custom tooling and connectors, increasing development effort and complexity.

title: Lack of robust tooling for local LLM development
problem: Developers need better first-class support and standardized tooling for working with local LLMs (e.g., Ollama, LM Studio). The current ecosystem often requires workarounds or lacks comprehensive frameworks, making it harder to develop and test applications using local models.

title: Ensuring safety and security of AI agents
problem: A significant concern for developers is ensuring that AI agents do not possess or develop dangerous capabilities, especially when deployed in sensitive environments. Tools and methods for scanning and evaluating agent safety are needed to prevent misuse or unintended harmful actions.

title: Inconsistent behavior and bugs in LLM frameworks
problem: Developers using LLM frameworks like LangChain are encountering bugs, such as incorrect fallback mechanisms for providers or violations of node execution order in agent workflows. These issues lead to unpredictable behavior and hinder reliable application development.

title: AI agents struggle with Microsoft Office files
problem: Developers building AI agents face a significant hurdle when these agents need to interact with Microsoft Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). There's a lack of robust, dedicated tools that allow AI agents to read, edit, and understand the complex structures within these proprietary file formats, limiting their practical application in many business environments.

title: Difficulty in evaluating and securing AI agents
problem: Developers are struggling with how to effectively scan and evaluate AI agents for dangerous capabilities or ensure their runtime integrity. This affects anyone deploying AI agents, as there's a clear need for tooling to assess potential risks, prevent misuse, and provide tamper-evident evidence of an agent's actions, which is crucial for safety and compliance.

title: Lack of local-first LLM desktop alternatives
problem: Developers and users are looking for open-source, local-first alternatives to popular cloud-based LLM desktop applications. The current offerings often require cloud access, raising concerns about data privacy, offline usability, and control over the models. This unmet need affects individuals and organizations who prefer to keep their data and processing on-premises.

title: Challenges with LangChain/LangGraph agent execution order
problem: Developers using LangChain/LangGraph for building AI agents are encountering issues with the violation of node execution order. This problem leads to unpredictable agent behavior and makes debugging and reliable orchestration of complex agent workflows difficult, impacting the stability and correctness of AI applications built with these frameworks.

title: Need for better web data cleaning models
problem: Developers working with web data for AI applications face challenges in cleaning and preparing this data effectively. There's a demand for specialized models and tools that can efficiently process and clean messy, unstructured web content, which is a common prerequisite for training and fine-tuning LLMs and other AI systems.

title: Lack of reliable AI agent safety and security tooling
problem: Developers building AI agents struggle with ensuring their agents are safe and secure, especially regarding dangerous capabilities or tamper-evident execution. This affects developers who need to deploy agents responsibly and verify their behavior.

title: Difficulty in controlling and orchestrating LLM agents
problem: Developers face challenges in effectively controlling the flow and execution order of LLM agents, especially within frameworks like LangGraph/LangChain. This leads to unpredictable behavior and makes complex agentic workflows difficult to manage and debug.

title: Lack of robust tools for AI agents to interact with Office files
problem: AI agents currently lack robust and reliable tools to programmatically read and edit Microsoft Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). This limits the ability of AI agents to automate tasks and integrate with common business workflows.

title: Challenges in cleaning and preparing web data for LLMs
problem: Developers need effective and efficient models and tools for cleaning and preparing web data, which is often noisy and unstructured, for use with LLMs. This is a recurring pain point for anyone working on web-scale data ingestion for AI applications.

title: Difficulty in visualizing and understanding LLM thought processes
problem: Developers struggle to visualize and understand the internal thought processes of LLMs, making it hard to debug, interpret, and improve their reasoning. This affects developers working on complex LLM applications and agentic systems.

title: Running LLMs on resource-constrained hardware
problem: Developers struggle to get large language models (LLMs) like GLM 5.2 to run efficiently on less powerful or older computers. This affects individual developers, researchers, and small teams who may not have access to high-end GPUs or cloud computing resources, limiting their ability to experiment and deploy models locally.

title: Lack of visibility into AI agent reasoning
problem: Developers lack tools to understand and debug what an AI agent 'thinks' before it produces an answer. This makes it difficult to diagnose errors, improve agent performance, and ensure reliability, impacting anyone building or deploying AI agents.

title: Integrating AI agents with web applications
problem: There's a recurring need for better methods to enable AI agents to interact with and control existing web applications. Developers are looking for ways to 'reverse-engineer' web apps into tools that agents can effectively use, which is crucial for automating tasks and extending agent capabilities.

title: Missing support for new LLM models in existing tools
problem: Newer LLM models, such as GPT-5.6 variants, are often not immediately supported by existing development tools, APIs, and frameworks. This forces developers to wait for updates or implement workarounds, hindering their ability to leverage the latest advancements in LLM technology.

title: Need for better AI agent orchestration and management
problem: Developers are seeking more robust ways to define, manage, and visualize the behavior and interactions of AI agents. This includes a need for declarative specifications (like Terraform for infrastructure) and better visualization tools to understand complex agent systems.

title: LLM agents cause data loss and instability
problem: Developers are experiencing critical issues with LLM agents, including accidental deletion of user files and silent skipping of crucial components, leading to data loss and unreliable application behavior. This directly impacts user trust and the stability of applications integrating these agents.

title: Difficulty integrating custom AI agents
problem: Developers face challenges when trying to use or integrate AI agents other than the default or most popular ones into their development environments and tools. This limits flexibility and choice, making it harder to leverage specialized agents or switch providers.

title: Frustration with AI agent development complexity
problem: Many developers find the process of coding and managing AI agents frustrating and complex, leading to feelings of alienation and questioning their own skill. This indicates a need for better tools, abstractions, or methodologies to simplify agent development and reduce cognitive load.

title: Inconsistent model availability across platforms
problem: Developers encounter situations where new or specific LLM models are available through certain APIs or CLIs but are missing from other providers or SDKs, even within the same ecosystem. This inconsistency complicates development workflows and forces workarounds to access desired models.

title: LLM Over-recommendation and Alienation
problem: Developers are frustrated by the pervasive suggestion to 'ask an LLM' for every problem, even when it's not the appropriate solution. This over-recommendation leads to a sense of alienation and a feeling that their expertise is being devalued, impacting morale and efficient problem-solving.

title: Managing and Orchestrating AI Agents
problem: There's a significant challenge in effectively managing and orchestrating multiple AI agents, especially concerning their interactions, memory strategies, and overall control. Developers need better tools and frameworks to define 'who manages the agents' and how they should operate cohesively.

title: High Token Consumption for AI Agents
problem: AI agents, particularly when processing large amounts of information like entire web pages, incur extremely high token costs. This makes complex tasks financially prohibitive and computationally inefficient for developers building agents that need to ingest extensive data.

title: Limited AI Agent Integration in IDEs
problem: Developers are struggling with the lack of flexibility in integrating and switching between different AI agents within their preferred Integrated Development Environments (IDEs). They are often locked into default agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio) and cannot easily configure or use alternatives.

title: API Key Resolution Issues for AI Services
problem: Developers encounter errors when using API keys for AI services, specifically related to actor resolution. The system fails to identify the 'activity consumer' associated with the API key, leading to 'PROJECT_MEMBER_NOT_FOUND' errors and preventing successful API calls.

title: LLMs process excessive tokens before prompt
problem: Developers are frustrated by LLMs, like Claude Code, consuming a large number of tokens (e.g., 33k) before even processing the user's prompt. This leads to increased costs and slower response times, impacting the efficiency and economic viability of applications built with these models.

title: Unpredictable and rising LLM operational costs
problem: Developers struggle with the unpredictable and often high operational costs associated with using LLMs in production. Factors like token consumption before prompt processing and varying model efficiencies (e.g., migrating to a newer model for cost savings) highlight a need for better cost predictability and optimization tools.

title: Lack of transparency in LLM processing
problem: Developers lack insight into the internal workings of LLMs, specifically what happens between submitting a prompt and receiving the first output. This 'black box' nature makes it difficult to debug issues, optimize performance, and understand the latency involved, hindering effective application development.

title: LLMs consume excessive tokens before processing prompts
problem: Developers are frustrated by LLMs, specifically Claude Code, consuming a large number of tokens (e.g., 33k) before even beginning to process the actual prompt. This leads to wasted computational resources and increased costs for developers and organizations using these models.

title: High cost and slow performance of AI agents
problem: Developers migrating production AI agents are concerned with the cost and performance efficiency of LLMs. While some migrations show improvements (e.g., 2.2x faster, 27% cheaper with GPT-5.6), the initial state or other models might be prohibitively expensive or slow, impacting deployment and operational costs for businesses.

title: Lack of tools for human-reviewed AI-written code
problem: There's a need for better tooling to integrate AI-generated code into human development workflows. Developers are looking for programming languages and environments that facilitate human review and validation of AI-written code, ensuring quality and control in AI-assisted development processes.

title: Inefficient streaming in AI agent runs
problem: Developers are encountering significant performance issues with streaming agent runs, where the full run context is re-serialized once per chunk. This O(n²) CPU complexity can pin a core on long streams, leading to severe performance bottlenecks and resource wastage for developers building real-time or continuous AI applications.

title: Difficulty sharing and managing AI skills
problem: Developers and teams struggle with effectively sharing and managing AI skills or models within their organizations. There's a need for intuitive tools that allow easy distribution and collaboration on AI capabilities, similar to how traditional files are shared, to foster team productivity and knowledge transfer.

title: Challenges in Agent Memory Persistence and State Management
problem: Developers struggle with reliably persisting agent state and memory across runs, especially when dealing with streaming outputs or unexpected cancellations. This leads to data loss and inconsistent agent behavior, impacting the robustness and reliability of agentic applications. Issues include database connection errors, lost state during cancellation, and difficulties with session persistence in streamable HTTP servers.

title: Lack of Robust Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication
problem: There's a clear need for better support for agent-to-agent communication and coordination, including standardized protocols and frameworks for multi-agent systems. Developers face challenges in enabling agents to dynamically interact, share context, and collectively achieve goals, as well as integrating different agent runtimes and ensuring compatibility across various LLM providers and proxies.

title: Inconsistent Tool Calling and Function Schema Handling
problem: Developers encounter issues with how tool definitions (e.g., JSON schema from docstrings) are processed and how tools are invoked by agents. This includes problems with dynamic tool addition/removal, inconsistent handling of Pydantic models for output parsing, and difficulties in ensuring compatibility of tool calling mechanisms across different LLM providers and frameworks.

title: Observability and Debugging Challenges in Agent Workflows
problem: Developers face difficulties in understanding and debugging complex agentic workflows, especially when subgraphs are involved or when issues arise during initialization or shutdown. There's a need for better visualization tools, structured logging, and integration with observability platforms like OpenTelemetry to trace agent execution, identify bottlenecks, and troubleshoot errors effectively.

title: Agent Ops and Deployment Complexity
problem: Deploying and operating agentic systems presents challenges related to infrastructure, environment configuration, and compatibility. Developers encounter issues with SSL errors, host header validation, environment variable handling, and ensuring consistent behavior across different operating systems and deployment environments (e.g., Docker, cloud). There's also a need for better support for horizontal scaling and secure credential management.

title: Reliable State Persistence and Checkpointing in Agent Orchestration
problem: Developers struggle with ensuring consistent state persistence and checkpointing in agent orchestration frameworks, especially when dealing with streaming data or unexpected run cancellations. This leads to data loss and difficulties in resuming agent execution reliably, impacting the robustness of long-running agentic systems.

title: Interoperability and Compatibility Across LLM Providers and APIs
problem: Developers face challenges in maintaining compatibility and consistent behavior when integrating various LLM providers, proxies, and their specific API implementations (e.g., OpenAI batch API, tool calling). This leads to fragmented development efforts and difficulties in switching between or combining different model services within agentic workflows.

title: Dynamic Tool Management and Protocol Standardization
problem: Developers need better mechanisms for dynamically adding, removing, and managing tools within agentic systems, especially in complex multi-agent scenarios. There's also a clear demand for standardized protocols (like MCP) for programmatic tool calling and execution, to improve interoperability and reduce boilerplate.

title: Observability and Debugging for Agentic Systems
problem: Developers struggle with debugging and gaining visibility into the internal workings of agentic systems, particularly when issues arise from initialization, state management, or unexpected process exits. This makes it difficult to diagnose problems and ensure the reliable operation of agents.

title: Agent Memory and Context Management Challenges
problem: Developers face issues with agent memory, including ensuring proper storage path configuration, handling access permissions, and managing context effectively, especially with tools and external services. This impacts the agent's ability to retain and utilize information consistently across interactions and environments.

title: Agent memory persistence and state management issues
problem: Developers struggle with reliably persisting agent state and memory across runs, especially when dealing with streaming data or distributed systems. This leads to data loss during cancellations, difficulties in horizontal scaling, and inconsistent behavior across different environments or versions, impacting the robustness and scalability of agentic applications.

title: Inconsistent tool calling and API compatibility across LLMs
problem: Developers face challenges ensuring consistent tool calling behavior and API compatibility when integrating various LLM providers, proxies, or custom tools. This includes issues with `bind_tools`, `with_structured_output`, and proper tool schema conversion, leading to `OutputParserException` errors and difficulties in building portable agent systems.

title: Lack of robust multi-agent coordination and A2A support
problem: Developers lack robust, native support for complex multi-agent coordination and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication within existing frameworks. This hinders the development of sophisticated agentic systems that require agents to interact, delegate tasks, and collaborate effectively, forcing developers to build custom solutions or work around limitations.

title: Tool orchestration and dynamic tool management limitations
problem: Developers struggle with dynamically adding or removing tools after an agent's creation and managing tool orchestration declaratively. This limitation makes it difficult to build flexible and adaptive agent systems that can respond to changing environments or user needs by modifying their available capabilities at runtime.

title: Observability and debugging challenges in agentic systems
problem: Developers face difficulties in observing the internal state and execution flow of agentic systems, especially when dealing with complex orchestrations or streaming data. The lack of integrated observability tools like OpenTelemetry and issues with visualizing subgraphs make debugging and understanding agent behavior a significant pain point.

title: Reliable state persistence and checkpointing
problem: Developers struggle with ensuring agent state is reliably persisted and checkpointed, especially during streaming operations or when using external databases. Issues like lost state on run cancellation or operational errors with database connections indicate a lack of robust and consistent memory management across different components and versions.

title: Inconsistent tool calling and API compatibility
problem: Developers face challenges with inconsistent tool calling behavior and API compatibility across different LLM providers, proxies, and agent frameworks. This includes issues where tools are not correctly recognized, dynamic tool management is lacking, or specific API features (like OpenAI batch API) are not fully supported, leading to unpredictable agent behavior and integration headaches.

title: Lack of robust multi-agent coordination features
problem: There's a clear need for more advanced features to facilitate complex interactions between multiple agents. Developers are requesting explicit support for agent-to-agent communication and persistent task execution in distributed agent runtimes, indicating current frameworks may not adequately support sophisticated multi-agent workflows.

title: Observability and evaluation for agentic systems
problem: Developers need better tools and methods to observe, trace, and evaluate the performance and behavior of agentic systems. This includes extracting user feedback from agent conversations, tracing agent execution paths, and understanding the costs associated with model usage, which are crucial for debugging, optimization, and improving agent reliability.

title: Deployment and operational challenges
problem: Developers encounter various operational challenges when deploying and running agentic systems, including issues with server initialization, session persistence for horizontal scaling, environment variable handling, and secure credential management. These problems highlight the need for more robust, production-ready infrastructure and clearer guidance for deploying agentic applications.

title: Inconsistent Tool-Calling and Schema Generation
problem: Developers struggle with inconsistent and incorrect tool schema generation, especially when dealing with Pydantic models, and face issues with tool compatibility across different LLM providers and frameworks. This leads to agents failing to call tools correctly or parse their outputs, impacting the reliability and portability of agentic systems.

title: Agent Memory and State Persistence Challenges
problem: Developers encounter significant problems with persisting agent state and memory, particularly when scaling or handling interruptions. Issues include data loss during run cancellations, difficulties with session persistence in streamable HTTP servers, and operational errors with database checkpoints, making it hard to build robust and scalable agentic applications.

title: Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication Gaps
problem: There's a clear need for better support for agent-to-agent (A2A) communication and coordination, including the ability to dynamically add or remove tools during agent execution. Developers are looking for more advanced primitives for orchestrating complex multi-agent workflows, which is currently a significant hurdle for building sophisticated agentic systems.

title: Observability and Debugging in Agent Workflows
problem: Developers face challenges in observing and debugging complex agent workflows, especially when subgraphs are involved or when dealing with streamed state. The lack of comprehensive observability tools, such as OpenTelemetry integration and clear visualization of execution paths, makes it difficult to understand agent behavior and diagnose issues.

title: API Inconsistencies and Integration Hurdles
problem: Developers frequently encounter issues with API compatibility and integration across different platforms and SDKs, leading to operational errors and unexpected behavior. This includes problems with batch processing, SSL errors in database connections, and 'request before initialization' errors, indicating a lack of robust and consistent API design and error handling.

title: Inconsistent state persistence and streaming in agentic systems
problem: Developers struggle with ensuring consistent state persistence, especially when streaming responses or handling cancellations in agentic workflows. This leads to data loss or unexpected behavior, particularly affecting those building robust, fault-tolerant agent orchestration layers where state needs to be reliably saved and restored.

title: Tool calling and schema generation complexities
problem: Generating accurate tool schemas from Python functions and ensuring consistent tool calling behavior across different LLM providers and frameworks is a significant pain point. Developers face issues with incorrect schema generation, lack of dynamic tool management, and inconsistent tool execution, hindering the reliability and flexibility of agentic systems.

title: Interoperability and compatibility across LLM providers and frameworks
problem: Developers face challenges ensuring compatibility and consistent behavior when integrating different LLM providers (e.g., OpenAI, OpenRouter, LiteLLM) and agent frameworks. This includes issues with API batching, token counting, and general model client integration, leading to fragmented development efforts and maintenance overhead.

title: Observability and debugging for agentic workflows
problem: Visualizing and debugging complex agentic workflows, especially those involving subgraphs or streaming, is difficult. Developers lack adequate tools for understanding the execution flow, identifying bottlenecks, and troubleshooting issues in real-time, impacting their ability to develop and optimize agents effectively.

title: Reliable memory and state management for agents
problem: Managing agent memory and state reliably, especially in distributed or horizontally scaled environments, presents significant challenges. Developers encounter issues with memory persistence, configuration, and access control, leading to inconsistent agent behavior and difficulties in deploying robust agentic systems.
